Author: @cleverboyx
Content:
It’s funny though. I suspect Apple and Samsung differ in their philosophy on photos as you have explored in videos where you took a photo of the moon and Samsung identified it as being the moon and then MANUFACTURED details that were NEVER in the actual photo without telling you so. Replacing your face is a version that. If you use Photoshop, there is a difference in machine learning and Ai, between “generative fill” and “content-aware fill”. One is an imaginative take on what might go where you indicated. The other is a computationally likely approximation of patterns, colors and shadows such that it appears to “fill” things in. 

I will say one more thing. Once, I had taken of photograph with me and my mom and wanted a version with just myself and her (excluding some other folks). I downloaded a magic erasure app, tickled at how it could possibly vanish those people in the image. 

I was shocked to find that my request at the time was more impossible than I realized. Where I had circled on the photo… even though the app clear demonstrated it could erase things… it gave up and created a virtual tarp it proceeded to drape over the undesirable elements in the photo. I laughed a lot that night seeing what could be erased and what couldn’t. But, I was amused  the fact that someone made the decision to come up with a digital tarp rather than raise the white flag. 

We are going to be having more and more conversions about what is a photo, what is a picture… and what does it mean for us to keep images of things that aren’t really what was there.
